newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: ALPINE SKIING-VON GRUENIGEN WINS WORLD CUP GIANT SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-VON GRUENIGEN WINS WORLD CUP GIANT SLALOM.

text.p: Switzerland's Michael Von Gruenigen surprised even himself on Sunday when he clinched a men's World Cup giant slalom by the huge margin of 1.64 seconds.
The World Cup holder in the discipline produced two near-perfect runs on the demanding Podkoren piste for a total time of two minutes 13.42 seconds and his second triumph of the season.
His usual smooth and elegant skiing style left Austria's Siegfried Voglreiter a distant second in 2:15.06 with Norwegian Kjetil-Andre Aamodt third in 2:15.78.

"I am amazed at how strong I was today. I was definitely not expecting to win by such a big margin," Von Gruenigen said. "It is a very difficult and bumpy hill, but such conditions have always favoured me."
"One of my goals has always been to win on all the classic giant slalom slopes. Now I have completed this list with my victory here and at Alta Badia (in December)."

"If you look at the golden book of ski racing then you can see that all the big names -- such as (Sweden's Ingemar) Stenmark -- have won here in Kranjska Gora," he said. "I am very proud to have my name on this list."
Last winter, the 27-year-old who now has nine World Cup victories won the classic giant slalom at Adelboden, Switzerland, en route to his maiden World Cup title in this discipline.

"My goals are to defend my giant slalom title and make a medal at the world championships (in Sestriere in February)," said Von Gruenigen, who took giant slalom and slalom bronze medals at the 1996 Sierra Nevada world championships..
The soft-spoken and likeable Swiss said he had undergone a change of attitude over the summer months: "I am putting less pressure on myself this season.
"To be good at championships is difficult, it depends on your condition of the day. But the best way to boost your confidence is to win many World Cup races."
Voglreiter was also amazed and delighted with his first-ever podium finish in a World Cup race.
"Four years ago, I came close to winning (a slalom) in Park City," said Voglreiter, who crashed out of the second run of the race in Utah after having a first leg lead.
"I was so devastated then that I needed a long time to recuperate and find my form again," he said. "Winning was what I always wanted and worked for."
Aamodt, overall World Cup champion in 1994, was content with third place.
"I felt good today and hope I continue feeling this way. I want to win a race this year," said Aamodt, who was also third this season in a giant slalom in Soelden and the ParkCity slalom.
Alpine skiing's biggest drawcard, Alberto Tomba, disappointed his many Italian fans in the Slovenian resort by crashing out late on the second run.
"La Bomba", in his first giant slalom appearance of the season, was seventh after the first descent.
"I am upset I didn't finish. I aimed to be in the top five. I wanted to make giant slalom points to retain my seeding in the top group.
"But I feel in good shape in giant slalom and feel I was just unlucky today," he said. "I did not feel comfortable in the first run and therefore attacked too much in the second."
The men's programme continues with a slalom in Kranjska Gora on Monday.
